eligibilitySummary.enUs: Sales taxes in the United States are imposed separately by state and local governments, with varying rates and taxable goods; there is no unified traveler consumption-tax refund scheme that can serve as a nationwide market policy.

sources.title: How to pay and get help with state and local taxes

observedFacts: USAGov states that sales tax is imposed by most states and municipalities, with rates and taxable goods varying by jurisdiction.
No nationwide traveler consumption-tax refund policy can be established from this federal guidance because sales-tax rules are state and local.
limitations: This national-market finding does not determine whether a particular state, city, retailer, or airport has a separate programme.
It does not establish retailer-specific pricing, sales-tax treatment, or any refund.
